citations.narrative:
The facility did not ensure every dog received timely dental care in accordance with their dental treatment program.
A VMO observed an adult dog, "Roberto", Microchip number 992021000009122, with signs of dental disease. The VMO
observed with a significant buildup of hard, brown organic debris on the back teeth, with smaller amounts of buildup on
the front teeth. The back right upper molar had an area of red gum recession and separation from the tooth. The VMO did
not observe loose teeth, signs of pain, or inappropriate body condition.
According to medical records, the attending veterinarian diagnosed significant dental disease in January 2025, which,
according to his program of veterinary care, requires a timely dental procedure with anesthesia. Several dogs received
dental procedures in 2025, but Roberto did not. In January 2026, the attending veterinarian recorded that Roberto still had
significant dental disease and that she might need to remove the abnormal molar described above.
The licensee stated that Roberto is scheduled for a dental procedure in two weeks, which is 19 months after his original
diagnosis and 7 months after his attending veterinarian identified an abnormal tooth that might require extraction.
Untreated dental disease can lead to infections and bone loss.
The facility must follow their written program of preventative care and treatment to ensure clean and healthy teeth, and
ensure this dog receives appropriate dental treatment by the attending veterinarian.
Correction date: August 31, 2026.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class A license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by October 3, 2026, or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
